en.name: Zongzi
en.summary: Cooked zongzi keep 1–2 days in the refrigerator at 5 °C or below, and about 6 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). Anything you will not eat within a couple of days should go into the freezer promptly rather than staying in the fridge.
en.pantry: Hanging a bundle of zongzi in the kitchen is the traditional habit and the dangerous one. Glutinous rice packed around fatty pork and salted egg yolk is a textbook Bacillus cereus food: the spores survive the long boil, and a bundle cooling slowly in a warm kitchen gives them exactly the conditions they need. Get them into the fridge or the freezer as soon as they stop steaming, rather than leaving them hanging until evening.
en.fridge: 1–2 days at 5 °C or below is the cap for cooked starchy food of this kind; beyond that they belong in the freezer rather than the fridge. Keep them wrapped in their leaves, in a covered container so they do not dry out. Reheat by steaming until the centre is genuinely hot — not just the outside. A zongzi reheated only on the surface is very easy to produce, because the leaves and the dense rice insulate the middle, and it is the classic post-Dragon-Boat-Festival cause of trouble.
en.freezer: About 6 months at −18 °C (0 °F) — a figure read across from cooked rice rather than published for zongzi. Move uneaten ones into the freezer as quickly as possible after cooking, at −18 °C or below. Do not read that 6 months as an invitation: home-wrapped zongzi are best eaten well inside it, because the flavour fades and the leaves lose their aroma long before the time is up. Thaw in the fridge, then steam or microwave until the centre is hot.
en.thawing: Thaw in the refrigerator, then steam or microwave until the centre is genuinely hot. Never thaw them on the counter, and never reheat one straight from frozen and assume the middle is done.
spoilage: A sour or fermented smell when the leaves are opened.
A slimy or sticky film on the rice.
Mould on the leaves or between the rice and the filling.
Rice that has gone ropy or pulls into strings.
tips: Do not hang them in the kitchen to cool; refrigerate or freeze them as soon as they stop steaming.
Freeze promptly at −18 °C or below rather than after a few days in the fridge.
Thaw in the fridge, then steam until the centre is hot.
Eat home-made ones well inside the freezer window; the leaf aroma fades early.

faq.q: How long do zongzi keep in the fridge?
faq.a: 1–2 days at 5 °C or below. Anything longer should be frozen instead.
Yes, about 6 months at −18 °C (0 °F) — a figure read across from cooked rice. Freeze them promptly, and thaw in the fridge before steaming.

faq.q: Is it enough to reheat a zongzi until it feels hot?
faq.a: No. The leaves and the dense glutinous rice insulate the middle. Steam or microwave until the centre itself is genuinely hot.

zh.name: 粽子
zh.summary: 煮好的粽子冷藏 5 °C 以下可放 1～2 天，冷凍 −18 °C 下約 6 個月。兩天內吃不完的，應該盡快移進冷凍庫，而不是繼續放冷藏。
zh.pantry: 把一串粽子掛在廚房裡，是最傳統、也最危險的習慣。糯米包著肥豬肉和鹹蛋黃，是教科書等級的仙人掌桿菌食品：孢子撐得過長時間水煮，而一串粽子在溫暖的廚房裡慢慢放涼，剛好給了它們需要的條件。請在不再冒蒸氣之後就盡快放進冰箱或冷凍庫，不要掛到晚上。
zh.fridge: 這一類熟澱粉食品的冷藏上限是 5 °C 以下 1～2 天；超過就該放冷凍而不是冷藏。請保留粽葉，裝進加蓋容器避免乾掉。回熱請用蒸的，蒸到中心真的熱透——不是只有外面熱。只有表面熱的粽子非常容易做出來，因為粽葉和緊實的糯米把中心包得很嚴實，而那正是端午節後最典型的出事原因。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下約 6 個月——這個數字是比照熟米飯得來的，不是為粽子公布的。吃不完的請在煮好後盡快移到 −18 °C 以下冷凍。但不要把 6 個月當成邀請：自家包的粽子最好在遠早於期限前吃掉，因為風味會衰退、粽葉的香氣也會先散掉。解凍請放冷藏，再蒸或微波到中心熱透。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏解凍，再蒸或微波到中心真的熱透。不要放室溫退冰，也不要直接從冷凍加熱就認定中間熟了。
spoilage: 剝開粽葉就聞到酸味或發酵味。
糯米表面出現黏滑、發黏的薄膜。
粽葉上或米與餡之間長霉。
米變得牽絲，拉開時會牽出細絲。
tips: 不要掛在廚房放涼，不冒蒸氣後就冷藏或冷凍。
盡快以 −18 °C 以下冷凍，而不是先在冷藏放好幾天。
先冷藏解凍，再蒸到中心熱透。
自家包的請遠早於期限前吃完，粽葉香氣散得快。

faq.a: 5 °C 以下 1～2 天。更久就該改成冷凍。
可以，−18 °C 下約 6 個月，這個數字是比照熟米飯得來的。請盡快冷凍，並先冷藏解凍再蒸。

faq.q: 粽子熱到外面燙手就夠了嗎？
faq.a: 不夠。粽葉和緊實的糯米會把中心包住。請蒸或微波到中心本身真的熱透。
